title: Economic Partnership, Political Coordination and Cooperation Agreement between the European Community and Mexico (2000)
executive_summary: The Economic Partnership, Political Coordination and Cooperation Agreement between the European Community (EC) and its Member States and the United Mexican States, signed in 1997 and effective from 2000, establishes a comprehensive framework to strengthen bilateral relations. The Agreement institutionalizes political dialogue, promotes progressive and reciprocal liberalization of trade in goods and services, and encourages capital movements and investment. It covers cooperation in diverse sectors including industry, financial services, agriculture, energy, transport, environment, education, culture, and human rights. The Agreement sets up a Joint Council and Joint Committee to oversee implementation, provides mechanisms for dispute resolution, and emphasizes respect for democratic principles and human rights as essential elements. It also includes provisions for data protection, consumer protection, and cooperation on combating drug trafficking and money laundering. The Agreement is open-ended, with provisions for expansion and adaptation to future developments.
characteristics: Comprehensive Framework: Establishes a broad partnership between the EU and Mexico, covering political dialogue, trade liberalization (goods, services, capital), investment, and cooperation in numerous sectors (e.g., industry, environment, education, science, technology, social affairs).
Democratic Principles: The agreement is underpinned by respect for democratic principles, human rights, and the rule of law, making these essential elements for cooperation.

Trade and Economic Integration: Provides for progressive, reciprocal liberalization of trade in goods and services, capital movements, and public procurement, in line with WTO rules, and includes provisions on competition, intellectual property, and customs cooperation.

Sectoral Cooperation: Encompasses cooperation in areas such as agriculture, mining, energy, transport, tourism, statistics, government modernization, combating drug trafficking, science and technology, education, culture, environment, fisheries, social affairs, and consumer protection.

Institutional Mechanisms: Establishes a Joint Council and Joint Committee to supervise implementation, resolve disputes, and adopt binding decisions, with the possibility of creating special committees.

Data Protection and Security: Includes commitments to high standards of personal data protection and allows for national security exceptions; also addresses cooperation on data protection, health, and combating money laundering.

Economic Actors: Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development

practical_applications: Establishment of a Joint Council at ministerial level to supervise the implementation of the Agreement, meet regularly, and address major bilateral and international issues of mutual interest.
Creation of a Joint Committee to assist the Joint Council, prepare its meetings, and potentially exercise delegated powers.
Provision for the establishment of special committees or bodies by the Joint Council to assist in its duties.
Institutionalization of intensified political dialogue between the European Union and Mexico, including regular ministerial meetings.
Framework for the progressive and reciprocal liberalisation of trade in goods and services, with the Joint Council empowered to decide on arrangements and timetables.
Gradual and mutual opening of government procurement markets on a reciprocal basis, with the Joint Council to decide on coverage, procedures, and use of information technology.
Mechanisms of cooperation and coordination among competition authorities, including mutual legal assistance, notification, consultation, and exchange of information.

Commitment to establish appropriate measures for the protection of intellectual property rights, including a consultation mechanism for resolving difficulties and detailed measures aligned with international standards.
Regular dialogue and cooperation on economic matters, including information exchange and periodic review of cooperation development.
Support for industrial cooperation through conferences, seminars, trade fairs, and technology-transfer projects, as well as support for modernization, innovation, and quality initiatives.

Promotion of reciprocal investment through information dissemination, support for legal frameworks (including agreements to prevent double taxation), and development of joint investment mechanisms, especially for SMEs.
Cooperation in the financial services sector, including exchanges of information on regulations, supervision, and control, and joint efforts to improve productivity and competitiveness.
Promotion of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through joint investments, information networks, and access to finance, utilizing existing programs such as ECIP, AL-INVEST, BRE, and BC-NET.
Customs cooperation to improve legal frameworks, including exchanges of information, training, official exchanges, simplification of procedures, and technical assistance.
Cooperation on information society and telecommunications, including joint research, pilot projects, regulatory dialogue, and reciprocal access to databases.
Harmonization of health, plant-health, and environmental standards in agriculture to facilitate trade, and development of joint projects in scientific research and human resources.
Cooperation in mining and energy sectors through information exchange, technology transfer, joint research, and promotion of investment.
Support for restructuring and modernization of transport systems, including training programs, technical assistance, and information exchange on satellite navigation.
Cooperation in tourism focused on sustainable development, safeguarding heritage, and improving training in the hotel industry.
Harmonization of statistical methods and practices for mutual use of trade and other statistics.
Cooperation in government and institutional modernization, including human resources training.
Joint actions to combat drug trafficking, money-laundering, and control of chemical precursors, including coordinated programs, research, and information exchange.
Scientific and technological cooperation through joint research projects, exchanges, and training, with emphasis on participation by higher education institutions and SMEs.
Cooperation in education and vocational training, including exchanges between universities and businesses, and use of the ALFA programme.
Promotion of cultural cooperation and joint initiatives in various cultural spheres.
Training programs and cooperation in the audiovisual sector, including co-production and distribution activities.
Exchange and dissemination of information in the field of information and communication.
Environmental cooperation to prevent degradation, promote sustainable management, develop joint research, and encourage mutual access to environmental programs.
Closer cooperation in fisheries, with the possibility of a sectoral agreement.
Dialogue and cooperation on social affairs and poverty, including consultations with civil society and support for job creation and vocational training.
Regional cooperation initiatives, especially in Central America and the Caribbean, to promote trade, environmental cooperation, and technological research.
Cooperation to support Central American refugees in Mexico and search for lasting solutions.
Joint projects to strengthen cooperation between electoral and human rights bodies.
Cooperation to refine and harmonize consumer protection systems, including information exchange and training.
Technical assistance and joint programs for personal data protection to avoid obstacles to trade.
Health cooperation through research projects, vocational training, and programs to improve health and social welfare.
Commitment to make available appropriate resources, including financial means, for cooperation objectives, and encouragement for the European Investment Bank to continue operations in Mexico.
Establishment of a dispute settlement procedure compatible with WTO provisions.

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Agreement shall institutionalise political dialogue, strengthen commercial and economic relations by means of the liberalisation of trade in conformity with the rules of the WTO and shall reinforce and broaden cooperation.
kpi_list.metric_name: Institutionalisation of Political Dialogue and Trade Liberalisation
kpi_list.target_description: Institutionalise political dialogue and progressively liberalise trade in goods and services in line with WTO rules
kpi_list.measurement_method: Establishment of dialogue mechanisms and adoption of trade liberalisation measures

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties agree to institutionalize an intensified political dialogue based on the principles referred to in Article 1 covering all bilateral and international matters of mutual interest and leading to closer consultation between the Parties within the context of the international organisations to which they both belong.
kpi_list.target_description: Institutionalise and intensify political dialogue covering all bilateral and international matters of mutual interest
kpi_list.measurement_method: Establishment and regular conduct of dialogue sessions

kpi_list.kpi_text: The objective of this Title is to establish a framework to encourage the development of trade in goods and services, including a bilateral and preferential, progressive and reciprocal liberalisation of trade in goods and services, taking into account the sensitive nature of certain products and service sectors and in accordance with the relevant WTO rules.
kpi_list.target_description: Establish a framework for progressive and reciprocal liberalisation of trade in goods and services
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption of framework and implementation of liberalisation measures

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties shall agree to the gradual and mutual opening of agreed government procurement markets on a reciprocal basis.
kpi_list.target_description: Gradual and mutual opening of government procurement markets
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption of arrangements and timetable for market opening

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties undertake to establish the appropriate measures with a view to ensuring an adequate and effective protection in accordance with the highest international standards, including effective means to enforce such rights.
kpi_list.target_description: Ensure adequate and effective protection of intellectual property rights in line with highest international standards
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption and enforcement of protection measures

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties shall promote a favourable environment for the development of small and medium-sized enterprises.
kpi_list.target_description: Promote a favourable environment for SME development
kpi_list.measurement_method: Implementation of support measures and facilitation of SME activities

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties undertake to cooperate on technical regulations and conformity assessment.
kpi_list.metric_name: Technical Regulations and Conformity Assessment Cooperation
kpi_list.target_description: Cooperate on technical regulations and conformity assessment
kpi_list.measurement_method: Establishment of cooperation mechanisms and joint activities

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties agree to promote the harmonisation of statistical methods and practice with a view to using, on a mutually acceptable basis, statistics on trade in goods and services and, more generally, on any area covered by this Agreement which lends itself to statistical processing.
kpi_list.target_description: Promote harmonisation of statistical methods and practices for trade and other relevant areas
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption of harmonised methods and mutual use of statistics

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties shall take the appropriate measures for cooperation and liaison, that they consider appropriate, to intensify their actions for the prevention and reduction of production, distribution and illegal consumption of drugs, in conformity with their respective internal legal regulations.
kpi_list.metric_name: Drug Trafficking and Consumption Reduction Cooperation
kpi_list.target_description: Intensify actions for prevention and reduction of drug production, distribution, and illegal consumption
kpi_list.measurement_method: Implementation of coordinated programmes and technical assistance

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Parties shall make available the appropriate resources, including financial means, insofar as their respective resources and regulations allow, in order to fulfil the cooperation objectives set out in this Agreement.
kpi_list.target_description: Make available appropriate resources, including financial means, to fulfil cooperation objectives
kpi_list.measurement_method: Provision and allocation of resources as per agreement

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union (referred to as the 'Community') is a principal party to the agreement, representing both itself and its Member States. It is central to the negotiation, implementation, and institutional framework of the agreement, and is repeatedly referenced throughout the text as a key decision-maker and actor in all major initiatives, including trade, cooperation, and political dialogue.

top_actors.name: United Mexican States
top_actors.justification: Mexico is the other principal party to the agreement, directly involved in all aspects of the treaty. The agreement is fundamentally a bilateral accord between the European Union (and its Member States) and Mexico, with Mexico participating in all key decisions, initiatives, and institutional structures established by the agreement.

top_actors.name: EU Member States
top_actors.justification: The EU Member States are explicitly listed as parties to the agreement and are integral to its implementation. They are involved in the Joint Council and other institutional mechanisms, and their individual and collective actions are necessary for the agreement's entry into force and ongoing operation. Their role is prominent in both the legal and practical execution of the agreement's provisions.

top_themes.name: Bi-regional Cooperation
top_themes.justification: Bi-regional cooperation is the central pillar of the agreement, as the entire document is structured around establishing and institutionalizing comprehensive cooperation between the European Community and Mexico. This theme is explicitly referenced in the agreement's objectives, scope, and throughout the detailed provisions on political, economic, and sectoral collaboration. It underpins the main message, occupies significant content, and is strategically vital for achieving the agreement's goals.

top_themes.name: Trade (including Digital Trade)
top_themes.justification: Trade liberalization—covering goods, services, and capital movements—is a core objective and occupies a large portion of the agreement. The document details mechanisms for progressive, reciprocal trade liberalization, including digital trade aspects, and links these to broader economic partnership goals. Trade is strategically crucial for economic integration and mutual growth, making it highly central to the agreement's commitments.

top_themes.name: Data Protection
top_themes.justification: Data protection is given a dedicated article, an annex, and is referenced in the context of digital transformation, trade, and cooperation. The agreement commits both parties to high standards of data protection, referencing international guidelines and EU directives. This is strategically important for enabling digital trade, safeguarding rights, and ensuring trust in cross-border digital cooperation, making it a key theme.
